semantics.definition: A near-side key produces a clear face-center division so one half is illuminated and the other half remains modeled shadow, while the head contour and shadow-side structure stay readable enough to distinguish the pattern from silhouette.
paraphrase_examples: One key set nearly ninety degrees to the side of the face creates a light-shadow division along the nose and face center, leaving one half clearly lit and the other in modeled shadow with readable eye contour, cheek, jaw, and head outline.

A nearly lateral ninety-degree key lights one facial half and shadows the other across a boundary that follows the central nose region, while both halves retain facial planes and the shadow-side eye contour, cheek, jaw, and head contour remain readable.

With one key approaching a right-angle side position relative to the face, the main light-shadow boundary follows the nose and face center; the lit half and shadow half stay distinct, and modeled shadow preserves the eye contour, cheek, jaw, and head outline.
A lateral key divides the same face at its center into a bright half and a modeled shadow half with readable facial contours.
측면 주광이 같은 얼굴 중앙을 기준으로 밝은 반쪽과 윤곽이 읽히는 그늘 반쪽을 구분한다.
